patterns.name: Point cloud starter (boxPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Minimal POP chain — a single boxPOP generator wired into an outPOP terminator inside a baseCOMP wrapper. Useful as the first step when learning POPs, or as a sanity check that your bridge + create + connect tools work.
patterns.notes: boxPOP generates a 6-face box mesh as points + topology. outPOP marks the chain endpoint — required for the POP family to be cookable when wrapped in a COMP and used as a Geometry source.
pitfalls: To visualize, attach a popViewer (COMP) or wire into a Geometry COMP feeding a Render TOP — outPOP alone produces no rendered output.

patterns.name: Noise-displaced grid (gridPOP → noisePOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Generate a flat point grid, then modulate the P (position) attribute via noisePOP. Canonical recipe for procedural surface displacement and the foundation for most audio-reactive or time-driven POP looks.
patterns.notes: noisePOP reads the P attribute from upstream and additively perturbs it (default behavior). Tune amplitude/period via noisePOP's params. To drive the noise period from a CHOP, expose the param as Custom and bind to a CHOP via export — or use a choptoPOP upstream to feed values per-point.
pitfalls: noisePOP modifies P by default; if the upstream chain doesn't carry P (rare for generators, possible for filter-only chains), the noise output is undefined.
Animating period vs amplitude gives very different looks: animating period feels like 'morphing terrain', animating amplitude feels like 'breathing'.

patterns.name: CHOP → POP cross-family bridge (constantCHOP + choptoPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Convert a CHOP's channel values into POP points/attributes via choptoPOP. Foundation for audio-reactive POP work — replace constantCHOP with audiofilterCHOP / analyzeCHOP / fft outputs to drive POP attributes from sound.
patterns.notes: choptoPOP has ZERO wire inputs — the CHOP source is bound via the `chop` param as a relative or absolute op path. The `src` value here is a sibling-relative path that TD resolves against c2p's parent. This is the convention for ALL cross-family ingestion POPs (choptoPOP, toptoPOP, dattoPOP, soptoPOP).
pitfalls: Wiring a CHOP into choptoPOP via td_connect_ops will fail or silently no-op — choptoPOP has 0 inputConnectors. Use td_set_param chop=<path> instead.
Path is resolved against the choptoPOP's parent, not the project root. If you move the pattern into a different wrapper, the relative path stays valid; absolute paths don't.

patterns.name: Noise-displaced sphere (spherePOP → noisePOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Sphere generator with noise displacement on P. Variant of noise_displaced_grid using a closed-topology sphere instead of a flat grid — the displacement reads radially-ish (because P starts on a sphere) rather than vertically, producing organic blob shapes well-suited to creature/asteroid/morph aesthetics.
patterns.notes: Same noise modifier as noise_displaced_grid but the input topology changes the look entirely. spherePOP has a `rows`/`cols` (or `divisions`) param controlling tessellation density — bump it for finer displacement detail. For perfectly spherical-feel displacement, set noisePOP to perturb along the normal rather than world axes (check the noisePOP `apply` / `direction` params).
pitfalls: Default sphere tessellation may be too coarse for visible noise detail — increase divisions before judging the result.
If the displaced sphere looks 'flattened' along one axis, the noise period is much smaller than the sphere radius along that axis. Either match scales or set noise to apply uniformly.

patterns.name: Grid with transform (gridPOP → transformPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Most basic affine modifier on a generated grid — translate, rotate, scale the point cloud as a whole. Building block when composing POP chains: drop a transformPOP between any generator and its consumer to reposition without touching the generator's params.
patterns.notes: transformPOP applies a single transform matrix to ALL points uniformly (rigid motion). For per-point variation use mathPOP or attributePOP with expressions. For animated transforms, expression-bind the t/r/s params to a CHOP or absTime.frame.
pitfalls: Rotating around the origin moves the cloud — if you want to rotate in-place, set pivot to the cloud's center first, OR use a precomputed centroid via attributePOP.
If you chain multiple transformPOPs, order matters (each applies relative to the previous result). Use a single transformPOP with combined tx/ty/tz/rx/ry/rz/sx/sy/sz when you can.

patterns.name: TOP → POP cross-family bridge (noiseTOP + toptoPOP → outPOP)
patterns.description: Convert a TOP's pixels into POP points (one point per pixel or sampled subset). Foundation for depth-to-points work, video-reactive particles, and any workflow where the visual source lives in TOP space.
patterns.notes: toptoPOP follows the same param-not-wire convention as choptoPOP — the source TOP is bound via `input0top` (note the indexed naming, hinting at multi-TOP variants). Swap noiseTOP for a kinectTOP or realsenseTOP / nidepthTOP to get true depth-to-points; swap for a moviefileinTOP to get video-driven points.
pitfalls: toptoPOP has 0 inputConnectors. Use td_set_param input0top=<path>, NOT td_connect_ops.

Default sampling reads ALL pixels — at 1920×1080 that's 2M points, which can tank framerate. Downsample the source TOP (resolutionTOP) before feeding into toptoPOP for interactive work, or set toptoPOP's sampling/density params.

patterns.name: Particle collisions with Ray POP (reflect + damp + mix)
patterns.description: Particle system where particles bounce off any collider geometry: rayPOP casts along particle velocity against the collider, mathcombinePOP computes a damped reflected velocity and mixes it in only when particles are close to the surface. Verified live against TD 2025 from elekktronaut Tutorial 78.
patterns.notes: The feedback loop is closed by particlePOP.targetpop pointing at the terminal nullPOP — forces applied downstream (reflect, turbulence) feed back into the next sim step. The mathcombinePOP does everything: velocity magnitude (MagV), reflected velocity from the ray hit (RayReflect x MagV), damping (x0.35), proximity gate (RayDistance < 0.25 -> Close), the conditional mix back into PartVel, and constant gravity via copya into PartForce. For audio reactivity, drive particlePOP.birthrate with an expression on a kick-detection CHOP (e.g. 4000 + op('kick')[0]*8000). Swap the collider spherePOP for any POP geometry (works with imported point clouds via pointfileinPOP + a mesh).
pitfalls: The ray-output attribute is 'RayReflect' (and 'RayDistance'), NOT 'ReflectedRay' — enable 'doreflectedray', 'hitnormal' and 'dist' on the rayPOP or the attributes simply don't exist and the mathcombine silently produces zeros.
particlePOP.targetpop MUST point at the end of the force chain (the nullPOP), not at the particlePOP itself — otherwise reflected velocities are computed but never applied.
A build is not done until a td_snapshot proves it renders: camera framing, weights left at 0 and fit/resolution crops all produce a black/flat frame with a perfectly correct POP chain underneath.
Damping 0.35 on the reflected velocity is the difference between particles that settle on the surface and particles that jitter forever — tune 0.2-0.5.
references: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X6RgNdsYMLA (elekktronaut - Particle Collisions with Ray POP, Tutorial 78)

patterns.name: Particle POP feedback loop (sim core)
patterns.description: The canonical POP particle-sim idiom: a point source feeds a particlePOP whose 'Target Feedback Loop POP' (targetpop) points at the null that CLOSES a transform/force chain. Ops inside the loop act per-frame and accumulate (spin, forces); ops wired after the null are stateless post-deform. Verified live rebuilding Okamirufu's Infinite 3D Point Vortex (900k particles @ 0.44ms cook).
patterns.notes: targetpop is set by NAME to the loop-closing null. Read the sim result from null_sim (or a selectPOP pointing at it) — anything wired after null_sim is outside the loop and does not accumulate. forceradialPOP emits a PartForce float3 attribute that particlePOP consumes on the next frame to integrate velocity/position. For an infinite-tunnel look, follow with noisePOP (combineentity=curl3d), a transformPOP driven by speedCHOP refs, and a limitPOP with z-axis Loop.
pitfalls: Tapping the render BEFORE null_sim reads pre-force positions — always tap the loop-closing null.
A transformPOP inside the loop accumulates every frame (rz 0.04 = constant spin); the same transform outside the loop is a static offset.
Steady-state particle count is min(maxparticles, birthrate*life) — birth 200k with life 5 saturates a 900k cap.
targetpop referencing a not-yet-created null silently no-ops — set it after the chain exists.
